Enter sends and Shift+Enter adds a line, and input methods for Japanese, Chinese and Korean are never interrupted. On touch screens Enter adds a line, since the keyboard has no Shift. Inserts go through the browser’s own undo stack, so ⌘Z always works, and long pastes become an attachment you can preview or put back inline.

The composer is the part of a chat people touch most, so every keystroke has to feel right. Prompt Input starts as one calm line with the + on the left and send on the right, grows into a card once the text wraps or files are added, and settles back when cleared.
The context ring opens on hover, click, Enter or Space, its label says how much of the context is used, and the breakdown is a table with a caption.
The effort control is a slider with a value text, and it keeps working with arrow keys and Home and End.
